pairs.subject: proactive-nudges
pairs.evidence: src/features/triggers/sub_triggers/UnattendedModeSection.tsx:8 Every trigger in this context is a user-authored rule (schedule, polling, webhook, file_watcher, clipboard, app_focus, composite) whose output is a persona run, not machine-initiated contact with a human, so the nudge-policy layer has nothing here to govern. A search of src/features/triggers/sub_triggers for nudge, proactive, quiet_hours, efficacy and attention found nothing. 'cooldown' hits only RateLimitControls.tsx:98, which is execution rate-limiting and belongs to scheduling. 'notify' hits only comments about the Rust file-watch crate.

techniques.evidence: src/features/triggers/sub_triggers/ActiveHoursSection.tsx:48 active_window limits the hours a trigger may fire a persona run (scheduling). It is not a quiet window on contact with a human.
src/features/triggers/sub_triggers/RateLimitControls.tsx:98 This per-trigger rate limit and cooldown cap executions. It is not a daily budget on interrupting a human.
src/features/triggers/sub_triggers/UnattendedModeSection.tsx:19 A trigger fires a run, held for approval or dry-run. No nudge evaluator produces a candidate notice for a person.

pairs.registryProposal: Agent-automation trigger UIs can carry 'active hours' and 'cooldown' controls that look like quiet-windows and attention-budgets vocabulary but govern execution, not contact. The golden path's alerting boundary could also name this scheduling-of-agent-runs neighbour so seats do not have to re-derive that it is out of scope.
